why: Holmes himself uses the name 'Madam Derbyshire' in this paragraph.
Holmes says twenty-two guineas is heavy for a single costume on the bill.

text: Who is the Madam Derbyshire of the bill?
why: The bill is made out to William Derbyshire, and Holmes's remark about 'Madam Derbyshire' invites the question of who she is.

text: Who is the Madam Derbyshire of the bill? — another woman
why: A plain possibility: by Mrs. Straker's account, the bill concerns a friend's household, so the costume's wearer would be some woman other than Mrs. Straker.
